sentences.text:
The first accused in C.C.No.1127/2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Kunnamangalam has filed this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash the proceedings against him in the said case.

entities.text:
Judicial First Class Magistrate Court,
Kunnamangalam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The allegation against him is that he, along with his wife, has committed the offence under Sections 420, 468, 471, 120B, 109 and Section 201 I.P.C read with Section 34 I.P.C in connection with the cheating committed with forged documents upon late P.T.Suresh Kumar, the husband of the de facto complainant.
The case against the wife of the petitioner, who was arraigned as the second accused, was quashed by this Court as per order dated 16.10.2018 in Crl.M.C.No.363/2017.

In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that none of the offences as alleged by the prosecution, are made out even if the entire allegations levelled in the final report are accepted in totality.

2. The prosecution case is that the petitioner fraudulently and dishonestly induced late P.T.Suresh Kumar, on the basis of a forged agreement, to believe that he would be given the profit share of the sale of a property of 16.32 cents of land at Ernakulam which the 2025:KER:19947 petitioner had agreed to purchase from CW5 to CW8 for resale at a higher price, and collected an amount of about Rs.71,00,000/- from the above said P.T.Suresh Kumar, and thereafter cheated him by not giving any such profit share or not returning the amount collected from him.
Late P.T.Suresh Kumar is said to have given Rs.30,00,000/- to the petitioner from the amount of Rs.40,00,000/- which he obtained by a sale agreement dated 13.10.2012 of his property.

A further amount of Rs.20,00,000/-
is said to have been paid by late P.T.Suresh Kumar to the petitioner out of the sale of the house which he had purchased from CW34.
An amount of Rs.11,00,000/- is said to have been paid by withdrawing the said amount by way of two cheques from IDBI Bank, Koduvally Branch.
Late P.T.Suresh Kumar is said to have obtained Rs.6,00,000/- from CW15, Rs.2,00,000/- from the brother of CW15 and Rs.2,00,000/- by selling the gold of CW10, CW11, CW12 and CW13.

It is stated that, when late P.T.Suresh Kumar realised that he was defrauded by the petitioner by showing forged agreement of the 16.32 cents belonging to CW5 to CW8, he demanded back the money paid to the petitioner, but the petitioner did not care to return the amount.

Thereafter, the dead body of P.T.Suresh Kumar was found 2025:KER:19947 under suspicious circumstances in a well in the premises of his house on 09.04.2013.
 3.
The case was registered on the basis of the complaint preferred by CW1, the wife of late P.T.Suresh Kumar, about his suspicious death consequent to the cheating perpetrated by the petitioner.
After the completion of the investigation, the Inspector of Police, Medical College Police Station, Kozhikode laid the final report before the learned Magistrate.

It is the aforesaid final report,
and the proceedings initiated on the basis of it by the Judicial First Class Magistrate,
Kunnamangalam, which the petitioner seeks to quash.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner committed the offence of cheating, forgery or criminal conspiracy as alleged by the prosecution.

It is further pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the second accused was exonerated by this Court as per order dated 16.10.2018 in Crl.M.C.No.363/2017, after realising that there is no basis for the prosecution case.

It is not possible to accept 2025:KER:19947 the aforesaid argument Sanjeev Kumar vs State Of Kerala on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187649822/
2 of the learned counsel for the petitioner in view of the final report and the accompanying records relied on by the investigating agency to substantiate the accusations levelled against the petitioner.

sentences.text: The allegation about the fraudulent and dishonest act of deception perpetrated by the petitioner upon late P.T.Suresh Kumar is sought to be established through the witnesses who are having direct knowledge about the aforesaid act of the petitioner.
The investigating agency is seen to have garnered the necessary documentary and oral evidence pertaining to the forgery and cheating attributed to the petitioner.

In addition to the wife, son and siblings of late P.T.Suresh Kumar, who are having direct knowledge about the transaction between the petitioner and late P.T.Suresh Kumar, CW5 to CW8 are arraigned in the final report to establish the fraud played by the petitioner by making use of a forged agreement to induce late P.T.Suresh Kumar to believe that he could get the profit share out of the sale of the 16.32 cents of land which the petitioner had purportedly agreed to purchase from CW5 to CW8.

It is not possible to brush aside the indictment in the final report and the accompanying records which the investigating agency has submitted before the 2025:KER:19947 learned Magistrate in support of the charge levelled against the petitioner.
The contention of the petitioner that the prosecution records would not make out any of the offences alleged in this case, is totally unfounded.
It is too premature for this Court to embark upon the acceptability of the materials mobilised by the prosecution to establish the charge levelled against the petitioner.
The truth or falsity of the aforesaid evidence are to be tested in the trial before the learned Magistrate.
At any rate, there is absolutely no scope for invoking the inherent powers of this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.
Accordingly, I find that there is absolutely no merit in the present petition.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed.

(sd/-)
 G. GIRISH, JUDGE jsr  2025:KER:19947
